choices.A: Because a pair of corresponding right angles is already equal, equal corresponding hypotenuses and legs form a special case of SSA, namely HL
choices.B: Because any two triangles are congruent if two sides and the angle opposite one of those sides are respectively equal
choices.C: Because the two acute angles of a right triangle are complementary, all three pairs of corresponding angles are equal
choices.D: Because the hypotenuse of a right triangle is always the shortest side

question: Why can SSA be used here for right triangles? (This refers to the fact that two right triangles are congruent if their hypotenuses and one pair of legs are respectively equal.)
solution: SSA does not establish congruence in general. However, in right triangles, the right angles (opposite the hypotenuses) are already equal, so equal corresponding hypotenuses and one pair of equal corresponding legs are sufficient for congruence. This is HL.
